source.title: MOMA: Masked Orthogonal Matrix Alignment for Zero-Additional-Parameter Model Merging
source.authors: Fanshuang Kong; Richong Zhang; Zhijie Nie; Hang Zhou; Ziqiao Wang; Qiang Sun; Chunming Hu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether a simple transformation can align merged and fine-tuned representations, using learned transformation constraints and representation-similarity measures rather than the original sources' methods.
record.gate_note: The paper directly fits transformations between merged and fine-tuned representations and reports their effects on representation similarity and task accuracy. Rows below cover the transformation and alignment results in Table 4 and Figures 4–5. Other model-merging benchmark results, KNN evaluations, and few-shot classifier-alignment results are not rows because they do not directly test the representation-mapping claim.
record.test_reason: The study does not test convergence between distinct models. It maps a merged encoder's representations back onto the fine-tuned encoders it was built from. These are Task Arithmetic, Weight Averaging or Ties merges of ViT-B/32 and BERT checkpoints sharing one base initialisation. The merged model is a linear combination of the target model's own weights, so alignability says nothing about independently trained models converging. It bears on drift within one weight-space family. The orthogonal-alignment probe (Sec. 3.3–3.4) is a diagnostic for the authors' merging method, MOMA, and the headline numbers (Tables 2–5) are that method's performance. These findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the merged encoder's degradation on classification stems from a predominantly orthogonal misalignment with the static task heads, not information loss. MOMA, which combines orthogonal maps absorbed into the heads with a task-vector mask, recovers near fine-tuned accuracy with zero added parameters or inference cost. The finding concerns merged vs. source fine-tuned models sharing one base, not distinct models.
record.recipe_differences: Learns orthogonal transformations and a task-vector mask for model merging; it is not a reproduction of either original source's convergence measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that adding masking improves on orthogonal alignment alone, while relaxing the transformation constraint to linear gives only marginal additional accuracy in the reported ablation.

fits_no_version.finding: After merging, the merged encoder's representations differ from each source fine-tuned encoder's mainly by a near-orthogonal map. Orthogonal-only alignment lifts ViT-B/32 Task Arithmetic from 69.1 to 76.4 (CV) and BERT from 64.3 to 72.3 (NLP). Cosine similarity moves toward 1 and coefficients approach 1, close to an unconstrained linear map. Looser maps add marginal gains.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation drift induced by weight-space merging of homologous fine-tuned models is approximately an orthogonal transformation, recoverable by a rotation with little loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding a learned task-vector mask to orthogonal alignment (MOMA) reaches near fine-tuned accuracy: 88.2 vs 90.5 on CV, 76.3 vs 76.3 on NLP. Linear plus masking gives 89.9 and 76.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Method performance of MOMA for model merging; not a convergence claim.

record.problems: The representation-alignment experiments concern merged and fine-tuned models in classification settings, not independently trained models spanning architectures or modalities. The authors' core similarity plots are figure-only in the supplied text and provide no exact values or uncertainty estimates. The paper reports uncertainty for other evaluations, but not for the central alignment results.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted unrelated model-merging benchmark tables, KNN classification results, and Aligned-C few-shot classifier results; these do not directly test whether a simple transformation maps one model's representations onto another's. Table 2, Table 3, Tables 5–10, and Figures 1–3 and 6–15.

untested.parts: No scale sweep and no independently trained models of differing architecture, objective or data.
No different-seed models; all models share one pre-trained initialisation.
No mapping between distinct, independently trained models; only merged encoders mapped back onto their own source fine-tuned encoders.
No variation of the similarity metric or input distribution aimed at convergence.
No test of the causes or plateau of cross-model alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are dropped because no row measures mapping between distinct models. Neither original source is cited. KNN and Aligned-C results (Tables 7–10) also concern merged models only. Figure 4 includes six transform families, but only orthogonal and linear are rowed; this is not needed for any version.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model scale or capability, and no comparison of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or training data.
No comparison of models trained from different random initializations to identify shared features or subspaces.

Tests learned transformations between merged and fine-tuned representations in classification tasks. Does not test stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired representation samples; does not test cross-architecture or cross-modal mappings.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified.
Does not systematically vary similarity metric settings, input distributions, or out-of-distribution data to test their effect on convergence.
Does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment, nor whether alignment between independent models plateaus or remains incomplete.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Task Arithmetic merged representations on the reported CV and NLP classification tasks, using orthogonal alignment with masking or linear alignment with masking
reader_labels.reason: The mapped models recover task accuracy close to the fine-tuned reference, and the reported cosine and coefficient analyses describe the orthogonally aligned representations as close to the linear-alignment result (r3-r6, r9-r24).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Orthogonal alignment without masking on the reported task averages
reader_labels.reason: Orthogonal alignment improves accuracy but is clearly below the full masked result on both CV and NLP task averages (r1-r2).
